description:
Implement a Stack Overflow benchmark using the publicly available Stack Exchange
data dumps. This benchmark provides a realistic multi-table OLAP workload based
on one of the world's largest Q&A platforms, featuring rich analytical patterns
including tag analysis, reputation systems, and temporal trends.

Stack Overflow is an excellent benchmark dataset because:
- Real-world data with natural distributions (highly skewed, long-tail)
- Multi-table schema with diverse join patterns
- Large scale: 630M+ rows across 7 tables, ~150-200 GB
- Rich analytical patterns: tags, reputation, temporal, text search
- Publicly accessible via multiple sources (BigQuery, ClickHouse, dumps)

Use cases covered:
- Tag popularity and co-occurrence analysis
- User reputation progression and engagement metrics
- Question/answer quality metrics
- Temporal trends and seasonal patterns
- Multi-table aggregations with complex joins

anti_patterns.dont: parse XML dumps at benchmark runtime
anti_patterns.instead: always pre-convert to Parquet in the data generation phase
anti_patterns.why: XML parsing is 10-100x slower than Parquet reads

anti_patterns.dont: require internet access for benchmark execution
anti_patterns.instead: only the data acquisition phase should download

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c "from benchbox.core.stackoverflow import StackOverflowBenchmark; print('OK')"

work_units.notes:
Options:
A) Download XML dumps and convert to Parquet
B) Export from BigQuery to GCS then download
C) Use ClickHouse pre-converted Parquet files

Recommendation: Option C (ClickHouse Parquet) for simplicity,
with Option B as fallback for freshest data

- so_score_distribution: Post score histogram
- so_acceptance_rate: Answer acceptance by tag
- so_view_answer_ratio: Views per answer
- so_edit_frequency: Edits per post by age

- so_user_impact: Combined reputation + votes + badges
- so_post_lifecycle: Creation -> votes -> edits timeline
- so_expert_identification: Multi-factor expertise scoring
- so_community_health: Aggregated engagement metrics

- Inherit from BaseBenchmark
- Handle multi-table data loading
- Manage foreign key relationships
- Implement phases: generate, load, warmup, power

- Add to platform_registry.py
- Add to benchbox run --benchmark stackoverflow
- Add scale factor validation

- Handle text search differences (Body, Comments)
- Handle datetime functions across platforms
- Handle string operations (Tags parsing)

- Schema parsing tests
- Query syntax validation
- Scale factor calculation tests

- DuckDB full workflow test
- Data loading verification
- Query execution and result validation

- Query catalog documentation
- Scale factor recommendations
- Platform compatibility matrix

Define dataclasses/schemas for all 7 tables:
- Posts: Id, PostTypeId, CreationDate, Score, ViewCount, Body, Title, Tags, OwnerUserId, AnswerCount
- Users: Id, Reputation, DisplayName, Views, UpVotes, DownVotes, Location, CreationDate
- Votes: Id, PostId, VoteTypeId, UserId, CreationDate
- Comments: Id, PostId, Score, Text, UserId, CreationDate
- Badges: Id, UserId, Name, Class, Date
- PostLinks: Id, PostId, RelatedPostId, LinkTypeId
- PostHistory: Id, PostId, PostHistoryTypeId, UserId, CreationDate

- Download from ClickHouse S3 bucket or similar source
- Validate checksums and file integrity
- Support incremental download for large files

- Time-based sampling (e.g., last N years)
- Maintain referential integrity across tables
- Generate reproducible subsets with seed

- DuckDB: Direct Parquet loading
- PostgreSQL: COPY from Parquet via DuckDB export
- ClickHouse: Native Parquet import
- Snowflake: Stage and COPY INTO
